appearance_dry: Not well recorded; the word yinhao, silver down, suggests a downy leaf, as with other teas of that name.
appearance_liquor: Typically pale yellow-green and clear, as with other Jiangsu spring greens.

description:
Erquan Yinhao is a green tea from Wuxi in Jiangsu, listed among the province's named teas alongside Dongting Biluochun and Nanjing Yuhua. Yinhao means silver down. Beyond that, very little is on record.

How it is made is not well described. It is a green tea, so the basics are those of its class: heat to stop oxidation, then shaping and drying.

There is no reliable tasting record to quote. Treat it as you would another tender Jiangsu green: water around 80°C, short steeps, and judge it for yourself.

If you find it, ask the seller for the picking date and where in the Wuxi area it comes from. Wuxi Hao Cha, another tea from the same city, appears on the same provincial lists and should not be assumed to be the same thing.
history: Little is documented about this tea: it appears on modern lists of well-known Jiangsu teas, but when it was created and by whom is not clear.
